locations.name: Pals

It suits your family well for markets and local food culture, nature access and small-scale hospitality, while staying closer to your preference for selective, lower-friction places than generic mass-tourism stops.

locations.name: Peratallada

locations.name: Sirvent

locations.name: Vejer de la Frontera

locations.description: Small Basque fishing town with strong food identity and a beautiful seafront setting. It fits your preferences for compact, character-rich places that combine scenery and everyday life.

locations.name: Zarautz
locations.description: Family-friendly Basque beach town that is easier and calmer than staying in the center of San Sebastián all day. Good stop for surf-town atmosphere without too much friction.

locations.name: Guéthary
locations.description: Small cliffside Basque village with a calmer, more design-forward feel than larger neighbouring resorts. It suits your family when you want an elegant coastal pause without excess.

locations.name: Saint-Jean-de-Luz
locations.description: Sheltered Basque seaside stop with beach, pastries, and market-town ease. A very good family route pause before crossing into France.

locations.name: Hossegor
locations.description: Low-key surf town with pines, villas, and enough family infrastructure to make it easy. It matches your taste for coastal places that feel established and characterful rather than over-programmed.

locations.name: Lac d'Hossegor
locations.description: Calmer counterpoint to the ocean beaches, good for an easy family walk or low-effort pause. Useful when the route needs a softer coastal stop before the inland drive.

locations.name: Collioure
locations.description: Compact painterly port with real Mediterranean character. Slight detour, but a strong scenic alternative when you want one especially distinctive stop on the France–Spain corridor.

locations.name: Cadaques
locations.description: Whitewashed, car-light village on the Cap de Creus peninsula. One of the most architecturally and atmospherically distinctive towns on the Costa Brava - resists mass-tourism better than almost anywhere else on this coast. Dali's house at Portlligat is a short walk away. A strong day-trip option from the Santa Cristina base.

photo.alt: Cadaques village on Cap de Creus

locations.name: Guernica (Gernika-Lumo)
locations.description: The most historically resonant town on the route. Market town in Biscay, seat of the Basque Parliament, home of the Gernikako Arbola (the ancient oak tree symbolising Basque freedoms), and the town bombed on 26 April 1937 that became the subject of Picasso's painting. A genuine half-day stop - not a drive-by.

photo.alt: Casa de Juntas and oak tree, Gernika

locations.name: Espelette
locations.description: French Basque village famous for the AOP piment d'Espelette. A short detour off the D918 between San Sebastian and Biarritz. The Espelette pepper cooperative sells directly - a tin is one of the most useful camp-cooking buys on the whole trip. The village turns red in late summer when peppers hang to dry from every facade. Worth 45 minutes.

photo.alt: Piment d'Espelette drying on facades in Espelette

locations.name: Camping Bachoc a la Ferme Pays Basque
locations.description: Farm-based campground in the French Basque countryside, rated 4.8. Quieter, more personal, less polished-touristic than the alternatives. One of the strongest hidden-gem matches on the whole route - the kind of small, family-run camp that fits the Snow Peak / Basecamps / wecamp sensibility without the brand. Good access to the French Basque coast (Guethary, Biarritz, Saint-Jean-de-Luz) and bus/train access back to San Sebastian as a day trip.

location.address: Bidart / Arbonne area, French Basque Country

editorial.summary: One of the 12 strongest campground candidates for this loop. Farm-based, quieter, more personal, rated 4.8 - replaces wecamp San Sebastian (3.7) as the Basque base.

photo.alt: French Basque coast near Bidart (Camping Bachoc area)

campground.notes: Farm setting, rural feel. Close to the French Basque coast and a short drive from Biarritz / Saint-Jean-de-Luz / Guethary.

family.notes: Farm animals and open space make it naturally kid-friendly.

locations.name: Parc Jouvet
locations.description: Large riverside city park in Valence with a big playground, a mini steam train, and a small enclosure with sheep and goats. Ideal mid-drive stretch break for kids on the Aix -> Provence leg - shaded, clean, free, with fountains and a playground rated 4.6 by thousands of families.

locations.name: Glaces de Maitre Artisan
locations.description: Tiny artisan ice cream shop on Rue Jean Jaures in Arles, rated 4.9 - unusual Provencal flavors (lavender, fig, calisson, black sesame, yuzu, cassis). A strong kid-friendly and adults-equally-happy stop for the Provence leg.

photo.alt: Arles Rue Jean Jaures artisan ice cream

locations.name: Camping Beauregard Plage
locations.description: Family-oriented campground directly on the beach in Marseillan-Plage (Bassin de Thau / Sete area). Rated 4.3 across 1200+ reviews, with premium pitches that include their own private shower and toilet. Abundant shade from pines, clean facilities, and direct beach access on one side and the resort amenities on the other. Much calmer than Cap d'Agde and much more authentic than the Sete port campgrounds. Good 2-night base for Sete market, Mont Saint-Clair viewpoint, and Bassin de Thau oysters.

editorial.summary: Best-fit family beach campground for the Sete / Bassin de Thau stop.

campground.notes: Direct beach access. Premium pitches with private bathroom available.

locations.name: Marseillan
locations.description: Small port village at the western end of the Bassin de Thau, 15 minutes from Sete and the home of Noilly Prat vermouth (free cellar tours). Small pedestrian streets, oyster bars on the quay, Tuesday morning market. Quieter and more authentic than Sete itself.

locations.name: La Fabrique a gout-the
locations.description: 4.8-rated artisan tea house / bakery in Marseillan village center. Home-made sandwiches, bagels, cookies, brownies, pancakes, and thoughtful breakfast selection - strong option for family brunch or picnic supplies before a beach day. Open 8am-6pm most days, closed Thursdays.

location.address: 1 Rue Achille Maffre de Bauge, 34340 Marseillan

locations.name: Chez Alphonse & Fils
locations.description: 4.8-rated hidden-gem ice cream shop on Rue Grand Rue Mario Roustan in Sete - small, family-run, with original Mediterranean flavors (sesame is the signature). Walkable from the Halles de Sete covered market. One stop, one ice cream each - exactly the right break for kids after provisioning.

locations.name: Olivier Bajard
locations.description: High-end French patissier's Collioure shop - world-class chocolates, glaces, and savoury lunch options. Perfect lunch-pastry stop on the Marseillan -> Santa Cristina drive, 5 minutes walk from Collioure's painted harbour.

locations.name: Casa Flora Girona
locations.description: 4.8-rated restaurant in Girona's old town, run by a local couple - fresh, well-balanced three-course menu for around 25EUR that regularly beats much more expensive options. Small, intimate, recommended by local guides. Perfect lunch stop on the SC -> Barcelona drive (or on a SC base day Girona trip).

photo.alt: Girona old town near Casa Flora

locations.name: El Palmeral de Elche
locations.description: UNESCO World Heritage palm grove in Elche - 200,000+ date palms descended from Arab irrigation systems. Vast shade, clean playgrounds, fountains, benches, public bathrooms. The single best mid-drive kid stop on the Valencia -> Cabo de Gata leg. Free entry, open 7am-11pm. Walking loop 1-3h depending on pace. 4.6 rating, 17,000+ reviews - consistently praised as family-perfect.

photo.alt: Palmeral de Elche UNESCO palm grove

family.notes: Shaded palm grove with playgrounds - ideal mid-drive family rest.

locations.name: Camping Lo Monte
locations.description: Large, well-established campground in Torre de la Horadada on the Costa Calida coast, ~255km south of Valencia and ~50km north of Cartagena. 4.3 rating with 3,000+ reviews - modern facilities, pool, gym, sauna, restaurant, clean bathrooms, bungalow rentals. Right at the Mediterranean. Good 1-night stop to break the Valencia -> Cabo de Gata leg and visit Cartagena as a half-day trip.

location.address: Av Comunidad Valenciana 157, 03191 Torre de la Horadada
location.formatted_address: Torre de la Horadada, Alicante, Spain

photo.alt: Torre de la Horadada beach near Camping Lo Monte

locations.name: Tiramisu-Gelateria
locations.description: 4.9-rated hidden-gem gelateria in Cartagena's old town on Calle Jabonerias. Creamy, generous scoops, English-speaking staff, slushies and coffee too. Perfect afternoon break while walking Cartagena's Roman theatre and old town.

photo.alt: Cartagena old town near Tiramisu gelateria

locations.name: Cartagena
locations.description: Ancient Mediterranean port city, founded by the Carthaginians, later a major Roman city. Walkable old town with a visible Roman Theatre, naval history museum, Modernista architecture, and strong seafood tradition. A surprisingly authentic Spanish coastal city - not touristy. Good half-day visit between Lo Monte and Cabo de Gata.

locations.name: Camping Caceres
locations.description: Well-run 129-pitch campground ~2km west of Caceres UNESCO old town, rated 4.4 with 3,400+ reviews. Each pitch has its own private sanitary block (shower, toilet, washbasin) - unusual and excellent. Pool, restaurant, good WiFi, bus stop opposite the gate into town. Strong 2-night base for the Extremadura leg.

photo.alt: Caceres old town near Camping Caceres

campground.notes: Private sanitary block per pitch. Bus into Caceres old town opposite the gate.

locations.name: Caceres old town (Ciudad Monumental)
locations.description: UNESCO World Heritage walled old town - one of the most complete medieval and Renaissance town centers in Europe. Stork nests on every tower, stone lanes, small plazas, Arab, Moorish, Roman and Jewish layers. Very walkable with kids. The Plaza Mayor just outside the walls is a great dinner stop.

locations.name: Borona Bistro
locations.description: 4.9-rated modern Spanish bistro in Caceres old town - tasting menu with wine pairings, consistently described as one of the best meals on any Extremadura trip. Small, intimate, professional service. Book ahead.

locations.name: Trujillo
locations.description: Hilltop conquistador town between Caceres and Monfrague. Plaza Mayor with the equestrian statue of Pizarro, medieval castle, storks on every roof. Smaller and quieter than Caceres, very photogenic, easy half-day with kids.

locations.name: Restaurante Dos Orillas Trujillo
locations.description: 4.7-rated restaurant hidden in Trujillo's old center, with a stunning plant-filled courtyard that stays several degrees cooler than outdoors. Perfect lunch stop on the Caceres base day or on the way to Salamanca. Small seasonal menu, local ingredients, very attentive staff.

locations.name: Parque Nacional de Monfrague
locations.description: Spain's most important raptor reserve - Griffon vultures, Egyptian vultures, black vultures, Bonelli's eagles, Spanish imperial eagles, black storks. The Salto del Gitano viewpoint gives eye-level views of nesting vultures across the Tagus gorge. A genuine wildlife-watching experience kids remember. 30km from Caceres - makes a half-day trip or a waypoint on the way to Salamanca.

location.address: Parque Nacional de Monfrague, 10695 Torrejon el Rubio

photo.alt: Salto del Gitano, Monfrague National Park

days.note: Drive day with selected routing, family-friendly stops, and the next confirmed sleep location.

Drive day to Provence (arrival). Scenic option takes you via Parc Jouvet in Valence - a large shaded park with playground, mini train, and sheep/goat enclosure - a much better kid-friendly stretch break than the usual autoroute aires.

routes.note: scenic route via Parc Jouvet (kid-friendly park) and Aix-en-Provence

days.note: Base day in Provence (day 2 of 2). Morning: Arles (Roman amphitheatre, Saturday market if timing works), then afternoon Les Baux-de-Provence. End with Glaces de Maitre Artisan ice cream in Arles - unusual Provencal flavors (fig, lavender, cassis).

Short transfer day from Provence to the Camargue wetlands. Quick morning stop at Fontvieille's Sentier des Moulins, then Parc Ornithologique de Pont-de-Gau (flamingos at eye level, wooden walkways - the best kid stop in the region). Settle in at Camping de la Brise, evening walk in Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer.

routes.note: scenic route via Arles (morning market if Saturday), Aigues-Mortes walls, Pont-de-Gau flamingos

days.note: Drive day from the Camargue to the Languedoc coast at Marseillan-Plage. Morning in the Camargue (flamingos at Pont-de-Gau before you leave), then a coastal drive to Sete for Halles de Sete market (fresh fish for camp cooking) and Chez Alphonse ice cream. Arrive at Camping Beauregard Plage, direct beach access for the afternoon.

routes.note: fast route direct via Montpellier bypass
scenic route via Aigues-Mortes salt flats, Sete market & ice cream
no highways route - small coastal roads past Espiguette and Sete

days.note: Base day on the Languedoc coast. Morning brunch at La Fabrique a gout-the in Marseillan village, then Noilly Prat cellar tour (for adults while kids snack). Afternoon on the beach at Marseillan-Plage or a quick run to Sete for Halles de Sete and the Mont Saint-Clair viewpoint. Evening oysters on the Marseillan quay (Bassin de Thau is France's biggest oyster basin).

Drive day from the Languedoc coast to the Costa Brava. Scenic option goes via Collioure (painted harbour, pastries at Olivier Bajard) and Figueres/Cadaques area before arriving at wecamp Santa Cristina.

routes.note: fast route via Narbonne and Perpignan
scenic route via Collioure (pastries at Olivier Bajard) and Girona
no highways route via Collioure and coastal Catalonia

days.note: Base day at wecamp Santa Cristina. Strong day-trip option to Cadaques on the Cap de Creus peninsula (~1h30 drive each way) - whitewashed village, Dali's Portlligat. Or stay closer with Peratallada's medieval stone lanes and Begur's cliff coves.
Base day at wecamp Santa Cristina. Easier-pace day after Cadaques: Cala Sant Pol for the morning, Pals rice fields and medieval village for lunch, Girona's Mercat del Lleo for evening provisions.

Short drive day to Barcelona. Stop in Girona for lunch at Casa Flora (intimate local restaurant, 25EUR three-course menu) then head to Barcelona in the afternoon. Evening: Mercat de Santa Caterina for provisions, Mies van der Rohe Pavilion at sunset.

routes.note: scenic route via Costa Brava villages and Girona lunch at Casa Flora

Drive day south to the Costa Calida. The standout mid-drive stop is El Palmeral de Elche - a UNESCO palm grove with shaded playgrounds and fountains, perfect for the kids to run and cool down. Arrive Camping Lo Monte (Torre de la Horadada) for the beach evening.

routes.note: scenic route with Elche palmeral break (shaded playground + UNESCO palm grove)
no highways route via Denia coast and Alicante

days.note: Drive day to the Cabo de Gata volcanic park. Morning detour into Cartagena for the Roman Theatre and Tiramisu-Gelateria (the old town is a genuine highlight - most people miss it). Then continue to wecamp Cabo de Gata through the semi-desert landscape of eastern Almeria.

routes.note: scenic route with Cartagena half-day (Roman theatre + old town + gelato)
no highways route via Cartagena and Mazarron coast

Direct inland route from Monte Gordo to Evora (skipping the SW Portugal coast we know well already). Short drive through Alentejo cork-oak country. Afternoon arrival leaves time to walk Evora's Roman temple and have dinner in the old town.

routes.note: scenic route via Monsaraz (medieval hilltop village) and the Alqueva lake

days.note: Base day at Orbitur Evora. Morning in Evora (Roman temple, cathedral, Chapel of Bones, Mercado Municipal for provisions). Afternoon day trip to Monsaraz hilltop village and Esporao wine estate (kids-friendly terrace, olive oil and wine tasting for adults).

Drive day to Extremadura. Cross into Spain via Elvas or Badajoz, continue to Caceres - one of the most complete medieval walled cities in Europe. Check in at Camping Caceres (private sanitary block per pitch is a rarity worth noting), then bus into the UNESCO old town for evening walk. Dinner at Borona Bistro if you reserve ahead.

routes.note: scenic route via Elvas (UNESCO border fortress town) and Merida (Roman ruins)

days.note: Base day in Caceres. Two strong options: (1) morning at Monfrague National Park - eye-level vulture colonies at Salto del Gitano, kids love this - then Trujillo lunch at Dos Orillas (hidden courtyard restaurant); or (2) full day in Caceres old town exploring the stork-topped towers and stone lanes.

Shorter drive than before (220km vs original 390km from Evora). Option to detour via Monfrague if you didn't do it on the base day, or stop in Plasencia for lunch. Afternoon arrival in Salamanca with time for a proper Plaza Mayor evening.

routes.note: scenic route via Monfrague National Park (vultures) and Plasencia
no highways route through Sierra de Gata villages

Drive day from Salamanca to the French Basque Country. The sleep location is Camping Bachoc a la Ferme (4.8 rating, farm setting) - a stronger match for the trip's aesthetic than wecamp San Sebastian. The scenic route takes you via Guernica (Gernika-Lumo) - the Basque parliament town, the oak tree, the historical weight of the place - and Getaria for txakoli and grilled fish at the harbour.

routes.note: fast route option - direct motorway via Burgos
scenic route - via Guernica (the historical stop), Chillida Leku sculpture park, and Getaria for txakoli and fish
no highways route option - slower, through northern Castile villages and the Basque coast

days.note: Base day at Camping Bachoc a la Ferme. The French Basque coast is right there: Guethary for the small-scale, stylish surf-village feel; Saint-Jean-de-Luz for the sheltered family beach and harbour-town pastry; Espelette inland for the piment cooperative - a tin is one of the most useful camp buys of the trip.

Short drive day from the French Basque Country into the Landes. Already on the French side so the border crossing is behind you. Stop at Espelette for the piment cooperative before continuing, Capbreton for fresh fish at the harbour quay, then settle into Huttopia Landes Sud's pine forest setting.

routes.note: fast route option - already in France, short direct drive up the Landes coast
scenic route - detour to Espelette for the piment cooperative, then north via Biarritz, Capbreton harbour and Hossegor lake
no highways route - small roads up the Landes coast with Espelette and the Hossegor lake

note: v3 update: Outbound compressed Provence to 2 nights and added a 2-night Languedoc coast base at Marseillan/Sete, plus a 1-night stop at Torre de la Horadada (Lo Monte) to break the Valencia-Cabo de Gata leg via Elche's palmeral. Drives kept 100-380km. Return now skips the SW Portugal coast (Sao Miguel) entirely and routes through inland Portugal/Spain: Monte Gordo -> Evora -> Caceres (UNESCO old town + Monfrague + Trujillo) -> Salamanca. New hidden-gem food and playground stops added throughout: Parc Jouvet (Valence playground), La Fabrique a gout-the (Marseillan), Chez Alphonse ice cream (Sete), Glaces de Maitre (Arles), Olivier Bajard (Collioure), Palmeral de Elche (UNESCO palm grove + shaded playground), Tiramisu-Gelateria (Cartagena), Borona Bistro (Caceres), Dos Orillas (Trujillo), Monfrague National Park.
